eyebrow: The Freedom to Choose Project · Year-End Campaign 2026 · Fundraising centerpiece · v2, told by Eloise and Eddie
title: Choosing Inner Freedom:
headline: No narrator. Two people who lived it tell it: Eloise, who was looking at a life sentence, and Eddie, who was lost. Both found something at their first workshop, both came home, and Eloise walked back into Chowchilla to give it to someone else.
story: This version is told only by people FTC changed, in their own words, like your inspiration reel. Eloise carries the story and Eddie answers her. There is no voice-over.

It opens on the stakes in their voices: <q>I was looking at a life sentence by means of my third strike</q> and <q>I was lost. I was hurt. I was in pain.</q> Then your intro. Then the first workshop: Eloise went with a friend who was serving life, and Eddie found <q>unconditional love</q> on a Sunday afternoon. <q>Maybe I can. Maybe I can. It started there at Chowchilla.</q>

They come home: <q>I've never heard you talk like that before.</q> <q>Where before I've taken, now I'm giving.</q> The climax is Eloise walking back into Chowchilla as a volunteer. First she tells us who Angela is: <q>the kindness and the compassion that I had never really seen in someone’s eyes until I met Angela.</q> Then she thanks her: <q>Your face and your heart has been with me all these years.</q> Eddie: <q>I have the freedom to choose. And I did.</q> Eloise lands the theme your narrative opened with, in her own words: people can push her buttons, <q>but my life doesn't have to be chaotic in my mind and in my heart.</q>
Eddie hands it to the viewer (<q>It changes your lives. It changed my life.</q>), then the ask, each part on its own slide: the $300,000 goal, the giving levels, Donate now.
do: Hook text at 0:00 already on screen (no animate-on): Eloise's own words in the split panel.
Slow it down: soft dissolves of 12–24 frames, and 1–2 s of picture after every key line.
Let the two voices carry everything. No narrator.
Cut every picture on the word it shows.
Faces, never backs. The people FTC serves first; volunteers only when they face the camera.
Show the speaker on the line that lands.
Only women on screen under Eloise's lines.
Dove top right from the logo moment to the ask; off on the Donate card.
ID card the first time each person is introduced.
Grade every source warm and natural before export.
Music 6–8 dB under the voices; near silence before the climax; the lift after “And I did.”
dont: No man in the black shirt (Gerardo), and nobody you have asked us not to show.
First names only. Eloise is a “Previously Incarcerated Participant”. The program is always “Freedom to Choose”.
No red; no black with yellow or orange.
No picture-in-picture: never Eloise, or anyone, boxed over moving video. Nobody walking behind a speaker.
No clip twice, and no b-roll or stills already used in the October reels.
No box or frame around faces, no stretched Zoom, no freeze frames.
No second music bed: mute the intro's audio.
No intro bumper, no logo on black, no full-frame logo card: the logo lives on the footage.

Eddie's times are in Eddie Torres_Raw Footage_GMT20231026-164006_Recording_640x360.mp4 (15:23). Eloise's are in raw_Eloise_Zoom_2023.mp4 (about 23 min). Times come from machine transcripts: the editor checks exact in and out points by ear. Every spoken word in this video is Eloise's or Eddie's. Pictures marked stand-in are FTC's own photos and footage from earlier FTC films, until your Female Participants and Volunteers folder is shared. Click any frame to see it large.

Your Oct 27 notes are in: no recording dates on screen · “prison” instead of Chowchilla on the graphics · first names back, so Angela’s tag reads “Angela · FTC Volunteer” · the Inner freedom slide now bridges to her words: “Rudeness and anger still come her way. Now she chooses how she responds.” · the goal slide reads JOIN OUR MISSION / Help us raise $300,000 by December 31 · “incarcerated” before student on every tier · no link on the last slide.

Ana Maria’s video notes (Oct 27) · her video · transcript (she reviewed the current cut; each row she talked about quotes her under Footage):
• Slow it down. “This is a long form video, not a reels.” Soft dissolves of 12–24 frames instead of fast hard cuts, slow pushes on photos, and 1–2 s of picture after every key line before the next voice. No shot under 3 s unless it lands on a word. About 2:50 is fine.
• New music. The current bed felt “trade show”, “elevator music”, “bubbly”, “commercial”. She wants it reflective and emotional, building to the climax. Options are in Files.
• Eloise alone. Never boxed over moving video. Her vertical picture sits on a soft blurred copy of itself, on the purple plate, or on the split screen. When her words need pictures, use full-frame photos: “This is great, just pictures.”
• Nobody moving behind a speaker (“that guy is walking by”).
• Faces, never backs. Show the people FTC serves; volunteers only when they face the camera.
• New row: who Angela was (01:38). Eloise names Angela before thanking her, so the climax has its bridge.
• Keep what she loved: the hook layout, “Maybe I can” on the hand-on-heart photo, the women in the yard, the Coming home split, “The prison she left”, the incarcerated tiers, the Donate photo.

decisions.t: Told by Eloise and Eddie, no narrator
decisions.b: You liked the buttons voice-over. We kept its idea and gave it to Eloise: <q>people can come at me with rudeness and anger… but my life doesn't have to be chaotic in my mind and in my heart.</q> If you want one narrator line back, say which row.
Eloise's story needs women on screen. The Female Participants and Volunteers folder is not shared with atdhe@happypeople.me. Please share it; the stand-in frames come from your own reel until then.

Her 2023 Zoom is small. If you have a better recording of her, or of another woman who finished the program and is home, send it. And is Eloise still an FTC Volunteer? Her title says so, from her 2023 interview.
Three 4K interviews from the Stockton workshop (DSC_6587, DSC_6588, DSC_6591) haven't been reviewed. If Eddie is in one, it replaces the Zoom.

The finished cut uses your approved footage, but the preview pictures on this page come from older FTC films. Is anyone in them former staff, or someone who signed a no-photo release? Tell us which frame and we will make sure they never appear.
Out of the video until we have the study (who ran it, years, how many women, how a return was counted).

One check on the giving levels from your sheet: the first three work out to $50 per incarcerated student per month, but $1,000 for 3 students for 6 months is about $56 a month and $2,500 for 8 students for 6 months is about $52. Keep them as written, or send the corrected lines?

You said the music felt like a trade show: too bubbly for a long film. The new bed is reflective and builds to the climax: Reviving by Megan Wofford. Backups: Gratitude and Finding Melody by Gavin Luke. Tell us if one feels right.
On the split screens (like Coming home), the panel carries Eloise’s words, so there are no captions under it. You said you’d run it by the team. Keep it that way, or add captions there too?
